summary: Declares that a role DEFINITION is a PROJECTION and never a document anybody writes. The defect it was built to make unreachable is not a duplicated file -- it is two files that are BOTH RIGHT: one role with two homes, each internally correct, drifting apart while every reader standing at either one sees no contradiction. So the kit ships ARCHETYPES, which say what is true of a role as a KIND wherever the discipline is practised, the host authors OVERLAYS, which say only what it legitimately says about its own instance, and the definition is composed from the two. The line is drawn by a test anyone can apply: can the sentence be written without naming a repository? If it can, it belongs to the archetype. The overlay schema closes itself to the archetype's vocabulary, so a host cannot restate a binding body even by accident -- the drift is not a discipline anyone is asked to keep, it is a state the schema cannot express. It ships zero of any host's content: no roster, no private knowledge, no answers. A host that has hired nobody projects a roll that SAYS SO, in those words, and an archetype nobody instanced is counted rather than omitted -- because a shipped role with no takers and a role that was never shipped read identically to anyone who is only shown what exists.

references.because: this role composes an archetype that neither the kit nor this host declares, so there is no body under the delta. The definition still renders -- it says UNBOUND, in those words -- and that is the surface being honest, not the defect being tolerated: a role whose base was renamed goes on carrying its overlay, and an overlay alone reads exactly like a complete role to anyone who only opens the file.
references.instead: declared as an archetype first -- in the kit if it is true of the discipline anywhere, in this host's own registry if it is not. A host-origin role is not an exception to the grammar; it is a base this host declares and an overlay that names it.
